chunks: My father, may Allah have mercy on him, said: Ali ibn Ibrahim narrated to us, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Yunus ibn Abd al-Rahman, from Hisham ibn Salim, who said: I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) say:
Allah has not been worshipped with anything more beloved to Him than Al-Khaba'a. I said: And what is Al-Khaba'a? He said: Taqiya.

key_terms.التَّقِيَّة: Taqiya, the practice of concealing one's faith or beliefs to avoid harm or persecution, considered a form of worship here
key_terms.الْخَبْء: Concealment or hiding, specifically referring to Taqiya in this context

ai.seo_question: What does the term Al-Khaba'a mean in Shia hadith and how is it related to worship?
ai.summary: In this narration from Shaykh al-Saduq’s *Mani al-Akhbar*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) identifies 'Al-Khaba'a' (hidden or secret acts) as Taqiya, elevating it from a mere political survival strategy to the most beloved form of worship to Allah. This highlights the Shia scholarly view that prudent concealment of faith during times of persecution is not just permissible but a high spiritual station, reflecting inner conviction and divine favor. The emphasis on 'hidden' worship underscores the value of sincerity and endurance when public declaration is dangerous.

en.basel-kadem: 1.	My father, may Allah grant him mercy, said: We were told by Ali bin Ibrahim, from Muhammed bin Isa, from Yunus ibn Abdil-Rahman, from Hisham bin Salem, that he said: I heard Abu Abdillah, peace be upon him, say:
Allah has not been worshipped with anything more beloved to him than Al-Khaba'a. I said: And what is Al-Khaba'a? He said: Taqiya.
